title: Wilmot water policy decision deferred amid Mannheim constraint
subtitle: Student residence purchase, hybrid bus order, bus stop snow clearing review and a defeated water working session.
overview: Council deferred its decision on whether to rescind the 1980 policy limiting water taking in Wilmot Township until March 25, 2026 {{vote:m5}}. Staff had proposed rescinding it so about 30 litres per second could be reassigned to the Mannheim Service Area, which has a water capacity constraint that has paused some development approvals. A councillor's alternative motion, which would only suspend the policy and add public monitoring and reporting, was also held over. Delegates raised concerns about drying wells and wetlands.

Council approved a Committee recommendation that directs staff to work with area municipalities on allocating up to half of capacity coming online within five years, and to develop a water conservation program {{vote:m13}}. After a closed session, it authorized buying two student residence buildings on Columbia Street West in Waterloo {{vote:m14}}. It also approved a $52.8 million hybrid bus order {{vote:m11}} and asked for a report on GRT bus stop winter maintenance {{vote:m20}}.

A proposed working session with the development industry was defeated {{vote:m18}}. Council also declined to waive notice for a motion on provincial water-taking permits, which was listed for the March 11 special meeting.

decisions.detail: Council deferred the staff recommendation to rescind the 1980 Wilmot water-taking policy, and a councillor's alternative motion to suspend it, to the March 25, 2026 meeting {{vote:m5}}.

Council directed staff to work with area municipalities on a risk-based approach to allocate up to fifty per cent of planned capacity coming online within five years, and to develop an enhanced water conservation program.

decisions.item: Waste by-law and bulky item collection
decisions.detail: The same committee report repealed the existing waste by-law in favour of a new one effective March 2, 2026, and directed staff to study less frequent bulky item collection and report by September 2026.
Council authorized buying 35 and 41 Columbia Street West for $7.3 million and $8.2 million, added $17.158M to the 2026 Housing capital program and one facilities maintenance position.
Council directed staff to explore a Facilities Strategic Plan and asked the Province to keep the Regional Chair elected or appointed by Regional Council and to consult before governance changes.
Council approved buying 34 hybrid buses from New Flyer Industries Canada at an estimated $52,844,190.26 plus taxes, with delivery expected in 2027.
Council asked the Commissioner of Transportation to report before winter 2026-2027 on options to improve bus stop snow clearing and on area maintenance agreement reviews.
Council defeated a motion for a one-day working session on water supply with Council, staff and development industry representatives {{vote:m18}}.

debate: Staff said Mannheim has been pumped above its sustainable rate for about three years, with monitored water levels approaching permit trigger levels. Some councillors asked why Council was not told sooner. Staff said the trend was hard to identify early and that the Wilmot Centre aquifer has more room than Mannheim's.

Delegates from Wilmot described dried wetlands and private wells running dry, and asked for stronger safeguards before any change. Staff said levels have been stable since 2019 and that dry years may explain surface changes, with a consultant review pending. Several councillors said they wanted region-wide data first, which led to the deferral.

Staff said the 30 litres per second from Wilmot already goes into the system, so the decision is mainly about allowing it to be counted for growth. One councillor questioned why Council had not been told of this earlier.

On the industry working session, supporters said it would build trust and transparency. Opponents cited staff workload across several existing working groups and quorum rules that would make it a Council meeting. They pointed to monthly special water meetings and planned public updates instead.

Delegates from the aggregate industry said washing operations recirculate most of their water. Councillors questioned the volumes on permit applications and the net loss, and raised concerns about rehabilitation. Separately, an industry association raised concerns about non-disclosure agreements for its water working group, and staff said corporate-style agreements were possible.
